body:
@shilman I recall that maybe there is already an issue about this? The issue here is the number control input (both in the control panel and in docs) doesn't update when the value of the arg changes "externally" (i.e. not via editing the control).

Similarly, if you simply change the args via URL arg, it affects the story but does not affect the controls panel / args table (So `useArgs` isn't the issue here, it's simply changing an arg's value *not* with the control in question).
@tmeasday Did you end up recalling what's the issue related to this? Perhaps I could follow/contribute to that.

issue.body:
This PR migrates stories for the `QuantitySelector` component and adds documentation for its props.

It also reverts a workaround introduced in #5354 in lieu of the official workaround recently published on the Storybook docs (see: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md#emotion11-quasi-compatibility).

Fixes #5367

### Testing

### Manual Testing

How to test the changes in this Pull Request:

1. Run `npm run storybook`
2. Explore the [QuantitySelector stories](http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/woocommerce-blocks-base-components-quantityselector--default). There should be two stories: a default one with the controlled component (i.e. can't set the values from the controls, but only from the action), a second one showing the component in its disabled state.

### User Facing Testing
These are steps for user testing (where "user" is someone interacting with this change that is not editing any code).
* [x] Same as above

body: @sunyatasattva I'm not sure if we found the issue, but the problem is reasonably contained as I understand it; the control's component is just not properly responsive to changes in arg value coming from "outside in" -- the classic React form state problem.

I think the bug is here: https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/lib/components/src/controls/Number.tsx#L31

We only use the value from "on high" to set the initial state. We need a useEffect hook that listens for changes to value and set the internal state based on this being changed.
PS if someone wants to look at it (which would be amazing!) the issue is likely there for (some of) the other controls also.
@tmeasday Hi i would like to work on this, please assign this to me.
